A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EpiNode and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. Content can be matched across the revised failure studies and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic epidemic experiments, ILI forecasting results, parameter inference, regional analyses, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original forecasting and ablation results and reports revised failure experiments and a new parameter sign-agreement comparison.

M1.justification: EpiNode retains the same VMD decomposition, channel extrapolation, delay embedding, collaborative latent ODEs, bounded rate decoding, SIRS integration, and training objective. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 show no procedural change; revised experimental alternatives belong to the comparison studies.

E1.justification: The five benchmark datasets and ten-region ILI coverage remain unchanged. Section 2 adds a fully observed SIRS scenario for the physics-informed model, extending the observability conditions tested. Changes to training fractions are protocol changes rather than new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Section 2.4 replaces the evaluated NCDE–ODE alternative with a mechanistic SIRS neural ODE whose rates are learned by neural networks. The former CDE encoder and residual-correction pipeline disappears from Appendix A. Comparator membership in the main forecasting benchmarks remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 replaces the stated per-parameter RMSE evaluation with sign agreement for time-varying rates and trajectory-based assessment for fixed rates. Appendix F removes the multiple-split schedule and the assertion that all reported metrics aggregate across those splits and seeds. These substantially revise the documented evaluation protocol without establishing that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 2 substantially revises its diagnostic experiments: ordinary and autoencoder NODEs are examined for failure under full observability, physics-informed models receive full-versus-partial observation controls under both SIR and SIRS, and the CDE case study is replaced. The explicit split-placement robustness report is removed, while the component ablations and regional analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean and standard deviation reporting over random seeds. However, v3 deletes Appendix F's statement that metrics pool across splits and seeds, removing information about the statistical aggregation basis. Table 2 follows the existing uncertainty convention; no increased run count or new significance test is reported.

E6.justification: The revised Section 2 plots support materially different findings, including failure under full observability where v2 described good performance. New Table 2 reports EpiNode sign agreement of 66.7%, 50.6%, and 41.3% for transmission, recovery, and immunity-loss changes. Section 4.5.1 corrects SIRS (Varying) TimeMixer++/LSTM values from 0.0219/0.0224 to 0.0550/0.1310 and attributes ILI values 0.0209/0.0219 to KAN-ODEs/EARTH. The main RMSE and appendix peak-error tables retain their numbers.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 introduces the definition of parameter-change sign agreement as the fraction of timesteps with matching inferred and true change directions. The principal VMD/ADMM, latent-ODE, and SIRS mathematics remains equivalent; the Dirac-delta and control-variable edits clarify notation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the performance claim to the strongest default-configured baseline and corrects the reduction range from 27–70% to 21–63%. The introduction reframes applicability from onset, peak, and post-peak phases to early-outbreak and multi-wave regimes. The central EpiNode contribution remains intact.

C2.justification: Section 2 changes the explanation of failure under full supervision and replaces the adjoint-based account with explicit bidirectional reconstruction. Section 4.6 interprets sign agreement as transmission-change tracking while acknowledging weaker recovery and immunity-loss inference. The conclusion removes the specific warning that recovery-rate estimates are not directly identifiable and the limitation concerning smoothing double peaks.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents mass-conservation and non-negativity constraints for the failure studies, five-step forward/backward reconstruction around sliding origins, and joint state/rate fitting with physics residuals at collocation points. These disclosures do not establish corresponding implementation changes. EpiNode's algorithm, hyperparameter-selection description, and code/data access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and methodological discussion substantially replace their supporting literature, including additions such as Cramer, Dureau, Boyd, and Rackauckas. The failure-study positioning shifts from Kidger's CDE framework to mechanistic neural ODEs, while several earlier sources disappear. This extends beyond bibliographic metadata corrections.

P1.justification: All four failure-mode discussions and their headings are extensively rewritten. The introduction, evaluation-metric paragraph, parameter-inference narrative, and conclusion also receive substantial revisions. The overall section hierarchy and most appendix prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 2–6 are substantially redrawn and reorganized, Table 2 is added, and the bidirectional architecture schematic is revised. The NCDE–ODE schematic and v2's split-schedule table are removed. Most forecasting, regional, and ablation plots retain their content despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Correcting the abstract's performance range, baseline attributions, and adjoint/bidirectional explanation improves internal consistency. Table 2 adds a useful quantitative check of parameter tracking. These gains modestly outweigh the loss of split-aggregation details and specific recovery-rate and double-peak caveats, which limit the overall improvement. The retained forecasting scores themselves do not improve.
